title: Gyroscope as an Inclination Sensor: Rotation Without Gravity

workspace.note: The EmbedStudio workspace the captures were recorded with, plus an 'Article figures' dashboard whose views are the ones the article's screenshots were taken from. elf_path and the SWD probe serial were cleared before publishing; neither is needed to review a capture.

attitude.gyro_angle_deg: theta[k+1] = theta[k] + omega[k] * dt, one accumulator per axis, dt measured per sample
attitude.gyro_initial_value: roll and pitch from the accelerometer, yaw = 0
attitude.computed: on-target, by the firmware, and recorded as the attitude_deg and gyro_angles_deg channels

integration_model.note: The three gyro axes are integrated independently. This is a deliberate simplification and is NOT a correct attitude estimator: body-frame angular rates and Euler-angle rates differ away from level, and the axes couple. The roll capture measures how much that costs.
integration_model.reset_rule: gyro_angles_deg is reset to the accelerometer attitude on every iteration while gyro_zero.ready is 0, and whenever gyro_init_request is set. Integration runs freely once the zero-offset estimate is ready.

captures.purpose: the integrator being released the moment the gyro zero-offset estimate becomes ready
captures.notes: The target restarts at about 1.9 s and every channel reads 0 for roughly 0.4 s. Before 4.499 s the gyro angle is reset every iteration and never differs from the accelerometer attitude by more than 0.04°; after it, the gyro roll moves 0.16° in twelve seconds while the accelerometer roll wanders over a 0.43° band.

captures.purpose: board rotated about the pitch axis past vertical and back
captures.notes: The rotation runs from about 8.5 s to 14 s. The accelerometer pitch cannot report past ±90°, so it folds back while its roll jumps to -176° to describe the same orientation; the integrated pitch passes through as one continuous number. Over 11-13 s the integrated roll stays inside a 0.55° band. A manual gyro_init_request reset occurs at about 5.0 s, before the rotation; the flag itself is cleared by the firmware faster than the host polls, so it reads 0 throughout.

captures.purpose: board rolled past vertical and back — and the axis coupling that comes with it
captures.notes: Rolling through 90° is NOT a singular orientation for atan2(a_y, a_z), and the two roll estimates agree to a median of 1.0° and to 2.5° at the 90th percentile. The disagreement that remains is mostly the accelerometer's: the board is hand-held and the acceleration magnitude reaches 1.28 g. The coupling is in the other axes — gyro pitch goes -11.94 -> -21.40 -> -11.79 and gyro yaw 0 -> +15.10 -> -6.56, an excursion that appears during the rotation and disappears afterwards.

captures.purpose: a full turn about the vertical axis, which the accelerometer cannot see
captures.notes: Turned by hand in four steps from about 8.7 s to 20 s, with plateaus at -82.5, -179.7, -251.3 and -346.3 degrees. There is no jig and no heading reference, so the plateaus are where the operator stopped and the total must NOT be read as a scale error. Accelerometer roll and pitch stay inside ±5° and ±8° for 98% of the rotation. The zero-offset estimator restarts at about 2.2 s and is ready again at 7.9 s.

captures.purpose: the drift measurement — five stationary minutes at steady temperature
captures.notes: Deviations are measured from the gyro angle at the sample where gyro_zero.ready first goes high, which is the accelerometer attitude at that instant. Over the same window the accelerometer attitude wanders over 0.49° in roll and 0.51° in pitch without going anywhere.

captures.purpose: the same measurement over three minutes, at a different orientation
captures.notes: gyro_zero.ready is 1 for the whole capture, so the reference is the first sample.

captures.purpose: stationary, with the temperature moving slightly
captures.notes: A 0.57 °C fall is worth 4.6° of roll in three minutes, against 0.67° over the same time with the temperature steady.

captures.purpose: stationary, with the sensor cooling from 38.5 °C
captures.notes: The board did not move: its accelerometer roll and pitch stay inside 0.8° and 0.5° bands throughout. ⚠️ This is a qualitative demonstration, NOT a temperature characterization. The cooling rate, the starting temperature and the gradient across the package were all uncontrolled, so no temperature coefficient may be derived from it.

channel_notes.gyro_dps.__struct.*: calibrated angular rate, the input to the integration
channel_notes.gyro_zero.ready: 0 while the zero-offset estimate is still being collected, 1 once it is applied

notes: The sensor samples at 1 kHz. Samples reach the host over SWD at roughly 275/s in these captures, which is the polling rate of the acquisition and not a property of the sensor.

Each variable is read in its own SWD transaction, so two channels recorded in the same row can come from firmware iterations a millisecond apart. During the fast hand-held sweeps the accelerometer traces also carry isolated single-sample excursions; compare those captures on the median rather than the peak.
The integration uses the per-sample measured interval from experiment #004, not a nominal one.
